signals.entity: MBH / Erste / K&H / OTP and the Act XVIII of 2025 ATM rollout (EKR coverage verdict)
signals.signal: Structural finding from an exhaustive sweep of the EKR public notice register (undocumented public API plus full-corpus CSV export, keyword filters on 'bankjegykiad', 'penzkiado', 'bankautomata', 'bankjegy', 'keszpenz', 'onkiszolgalo', 'penzfeldolgoz', 'ermeszaml', 'bankjegyszaml', 'automata', 'ATM'): ZERO ATM or banknote-handling procurement exists in EKR. MBH Bank, Erste Bank Hungary, K&H Bank, Takarekbank and Granit Bank return TOTAL 0 as contracting authorities; OTP Bank Nyrt. appears only as a subsidised buyer of building-construction works (2019-2020, 'Szerkezetepitesi munkalatok'). All 11 EKR hits for the string 'ATM' belong to HungaroControl and mean Air Traffic Management.
signals.source_name: EKR (Elektronikus Kozbeszerzesi Rendszer) public notice register
signals.implies: The ~600-631 Phase-2 ATMs mandated for settlements of 500-1,000 people by 31/12/2026 will NOT be tendered publicly - Hungarian commercial banks sit outside the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). Printec must approach Hungary's ATM/self-service opportunity through direct commercial sales to the nine mandated banks, not through EKR monitoring. EKR is worth watching in Hungary only for MNB, Magyar Allamkincstar, Magyar Posta, ORFK/NISZ and municipal/transport POS-and-cash items.
signals.likelihood: Very high - a legal-structure fact, not a forecast
signals.followup: Reassign Hungary ATM coverage from portal-watching to direct bank procurement contact (OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, CIB, UniCredit, Granit, MagNet) and to MNB decree/enforcement monitoring.

signals.entity: Hungarian banking sector / new Tisza-led government
signals.signal: The ATM installation mandate survived the change of government. Banks must still install roughly 600 ATMs in settlements of 500-1,000 residents by 31/12/2026. Banks have started but recently slowed down, hoping for a regulatory easing that has not come. Reported cost per machine: roughly HUF 8-10 million for installation plus a year of operation; banks complain the rural machines see only 0-2 withdrawals a day.
signals.source_name: Telex (Bruckner Gergely), 'A Tisza es a bankok: a kamatstopnak vege lehet, a babavaro halasztva, az ATM-telepites folytatodik'
signals.implies: Phase 2 is live and behind schedule with under five months to the 31/12/2026 deadline - the classic conditions for late, urgent, turnkey orders. Printec's play is a low-TCO rural ATM package (compact dispenser or recycler + site build + cash-in-transit + first/second-line maintenance + monitoring) sold as opex per site, exactly the 'ATM-as-a-service' model that answers the banks' 0-2-transactions-a-day economics complaint.
signals.likelihood: High that banks place catch-up orders in Q3-Q4 2026
signals.followup: Pitch a managed rural-ATM package (per-site monthly fee) to OTP, MBH, K&H and Erste Hungary procurement before end-Q3 2026; benchmark against the quoted HUF 8-10m per-site all-in cost.

signals.signal: MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), issued under Act XVIII of 2025 (ATMtv.) and NGM decree 16/2025 (V. 29.), names settlement-by-settlement which payment service provider must install and operate an ATM. Reported allocation across nine banks over ~913 settlements: OTP 383, MBH 147, K&H 102, Erste 93, Raiffeisen 64, CIB 52, UniCredit 46, Granit 13, MagNet 13. Verified from the consolidated decree text: banks may swap settlement packages or assume each other's obligations by contract; the deadline for such contracts was 20/07/2025 for Phase-1 settlements and 28/02/2026 for the Phase-2 (500-1,000 population) settlements, with notification to MNB via the ERA system by 31/07/2025 and 16/03/2026 respectively. Any operation-assumption contract must run at least 5 years.
signals.source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabalytar / Jogtar consolidated text of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.) (PDF, effective 27/06/2025); per-bank counts via Bank360
signals.implies: A named, quantified, per-bank demand list plus a legally-mandated minimum 5-year term for outsourced ATM operation - the single most useful targeting document for Printec in Hungary. The 5-year floor makes a managed-service contract structurally attractive to the banks that want to offload rural sites.
signals.likelihood: Phase-2 swap contracts already signed (deadline 28/02/2026); hardware/operations still being placed
signals.followup: Obtain Annex 1 (settlement packages) of the consolidated decree and cross-reference with MNB's ERA notifications to see which bank actually ended up owing each Phase-2 settlement after the 28/02/2026 swaps.

signals.signal: MNB data: 5,688 ATMs in Hungary at 31/03/2026, up from 5,211 a year earlier (+477 units, +9.15%); 5,437 at end-September 2025; the 2022 trough was 4,738. Growth is concentrated in rural counties (Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg +37.37%, Nograd +36.36%, Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen +24.6%) while Budapest lost 8 machines. Press estimate of the total mandate: ~1,039 new ATMs, ~HUF 4.156bn at ~HUF 4m/unit, split OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104, Raiffeisen 65, CIB 52, UniCredit 52, Granit 13, MagNet 13; reported installs to early 2026 were MBH 316, OTP 128, K&H 92. Existing fleets: OTP ~2,000, MBH ~1,200, K&H 639, Erste 491. Cash withdrawals are falling (85.7m in 2024; 60.4m in the first nine months of 2025, -6% y/y).
signals.source_name: Bankmonitor 'Hol telepitettek ATM-et a bankok az elmult evben?' and mfor.hu 'Teleszortak ATM-mel a videket a bankok, de csokken az igeny' (both citing MNB data); Penzcentrum per-bank cost table
signals.implies: A verified ~477-unit-a-year installed-base expansion in a market where transaction volumes are declining. That combination pushes banks toward the cheapest possible per-site economics - dispense-only compact ATMs, shared/white-label operation and outsourced servicing - all core Printec ATM and managed-services territory. It also flags a servicing annuity: ~1,000 brand-new rural machines needing first/second-line maintenance and CIT from 2026 onward.
signals.likelihood: Servicing demand is certain; the question is who holds the contracts
signals.followup: Confirm the Q2-2026 MNB ATM count when the payment-statistics release lands, and identify which vendors (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Euronet, Payten) took the Phase-1 hardware and servicing.

signals.entity: OTP Bank Nyrt. + Erste Bank Hungary + Raiffeisen Bank (Constitutional Court challenge)
signals.signal: OTP announced via the Budapest Stock Exchange on 10/11/2025 (after close) that it, together with other credit institutions - reported as Erste and Raiffeisen - filed a constitutional complaint asking the Constitutional Court (Alkotmanybirosag) to strike down Act XVIII of 2025 on ATM installation, NGM decree 16/2025 (V. 29.), MNB decrees 19/2025 (VI. 26.) and 20/2025 (VI. 26.), and the amendment of MNB decree 1/2023 (I. 17.). Grounds: the obligation is economically unjustified, disproportionately restricts the applicants' freedom of enterprise and right to property, and discriminatorily interferes with market processes. STATUS AT 01/08/2026: no Constitutional Court decision on the ATM law has been published; the mandate remains in force and, per Telex 15/06/2026, the banks 'have achieved no relaxation'. The Court's own case search (alkotmanybirosag.hu) is JS-rendered and returned no readable result for 'bankjegykiado'.
signals.source_name: Index.hu (reporting OTP's BSE disclosure) + Telex 15/06/2026 for current status
signals.implies: The legal challenge is NOT a reason to hold back on Hungary. With no ruling after ~9 months and the deadline 5 months away, the banks must buy. If the Court ever annulled the mandate the downside for Printec would be lost pipeline, not lost investment - the risk sits with the banks, which is itself an argument for selling them opex-based managed ATM service rather than capex hardware.
signals.likelihood: No ruling expected before the 31/12/2026 Phase-2 deadline
signals.followup: Monitor alkotmanybirosag.hu plenary agendas and OTP's BSE disclosures for the case number and any decision; note MNB 20/2025 amends the banknote processing/recirculation and counterfeit-protection decree 1/2023, which governs the equipment banks may use to recycle cash.

signals.entity: MNB enforcement regime for the ATM mandate
signals.signal: Payment service providers that miss the installation deadlines face escalating fines: from HUF 5 million after the first three months, rising quarterly, up to HUF 150 million after 24 months of non-compliance. MNB's methodological guide of 07/08/2025 on cash handling, processing and recirculation and cash-supply security explicitly incorporates the ATMtv. (Act XVIII of 2025), government decree 129/2025 (VI. 5.) on emergency maintenance of ATM operation (which replaced the repealed 49/2025 (III. 24.)), and MNB decree 19/2025 among the rules supervised entities must meet.
signals.source_name: MNB 'Modszertani utmutato a keszpenzforgalmazassal, -feldolgozassal es -visszaforgatassal, valamint a keszpenzellatas biztonsagaval kapcsolatos jogszabalyi rendelkezesek es jegybanki elvarasok teljesitesehez' (PDF, revised 07/08/2025); penalty schedule via Hungarian press summary
signals.implies: Hard financial pressure that converts the ATM mandate from a nice-to-have into a compliance purchase with a fixed date. A vendor that can guarantee installation and go-live before 31/12/2026 has real pricing power in Q3-Q4 2026 - Printec should lead with delivery-date certainty, not price.
signals.likelihood: Fines become live from Q1 2027 for missed Phase-2 sites
signals.followup: Verify the exact penalty schedule against the text of ATMtv. and MNB supervisory practice; use it as the commercial hook in bank conversations.

signals.signal: OPEN EU-regime open procedure 'Halozati kulcstarolo eszkozok es gyartoi tamogatas' (network key-storage devices + vendor support): new Entrust nShield 5c mid network HSMs with fixed and optional licences, hardware/software components and 36 months of vendor licence maintenance after delivery. CPV 48730000 (security software package). EKR001466692026, KE 12701/2026, TED 511411-2026, OJ S 140/2026. Deadline for tenders 24/08/2026 10:00 CEST, bid validity 30 days. No estimated value published; bidders must carry professional liability insurance of at least HUF 41,000,000 per year. Four Budapest delivery sites. MNB ran a preliminary market consultation beforehand under EKR001367012026. A parallel national-regime procedure, 'NSS es HSM eszkozok tamogatasi, konzultacios szolg.' (KE 10711/2026, EKR001193282026), closed on 14/07/2026 with no result notice published yet.
signals.source_name: TED notice 511411-2026 (PDF) cross-checked against the EKR public notice register
signals.implies: The only genuinely bid-able Hungarian public tender in Printec's core scope this cycle: HSM/security hardware plus a 3-year support tail at a central bank. Brand-specified (nShield 5c mid), so the opening is for an Entrust-authorised integrator with Hungarian public-procurement standing, not for an alternative HSM brand. The separate HSM support/consultancy stream is a recurring managed-services annuity.
signals.likelihood: Award expected within 2-4 months of the 24/08/2026 deadline
signals.followup: Confirm Printec's Entrust nShield partner status in Hungary and, if viable, download the EKR001466692026 documentation and decide bid/no-bid before 24/08/2026. Separately poll EKR for the result notice on EKR001193282026 to name MNB's incumbent HSM services supplier.

signals.entity: BKK Budapesti Kozlekedesi Kozpont Zrt. (competitor win)
signals.signal: AWARDED 22/06/2026: 'Bankkartyaelfogadas POS terminalok' - card acceptance across BKK's personal sales/customer-service network, its TVM ticket-vending machine estate and on-board fare inspection, covering supply, installation, operation and terminal management of POS, mPOS and softPOS terminals, acquiring for the self-service TVM POS terminals, Mastercard/VISA plus phased JCB and CUP acceptance, 24x7 merchant and technical helpdesk, transaction analytics and provision of the Qvik instant-payment service. Winner: consortium led by SimplePay Zrt. (reg. 32835155244, Vaci ut 135-139, Budapest) with OTP Bank Nyrt. (reg. 10537914444). Tender value HUF 1,318,733,639 (about EUR 3.3m). TED 424870-2026, OJ S 118/2026, prior notice 23750-2026, EKR002466592025.
signals.implies: A benchmark competitor win in Printec's POS/acquiring and self-service space in Hungary: the OTP/SimplePay pairing takes the country's largest public-transport card-acceptance estate, bundling softPOS and the Qvik QR instant-payment scheme. Confirms that Hungarian public POS deals are won by bank-plus-PSP consortia, so Printec would need a Hungarian acquiring partner to compete. Also a template for the equivalent BKK/transport POS renewals elsewhere in the region.
signals.likelihood: Contract now running; next renewal cycle roughly 2029-2030 on the 2023/2026 pattern
signals.followup: Log SimplePay Zrt. + OTP as the Hungarian POS/acquiring incumbent for public-sector estates; check whether Qvik (Hungary's instant-payment QR scheme) is a required feature Printec's POS stack supports.

signals.signal: 'ABC kapu, kioszk es biometrikus felvetelezo pont' - EU Entry/Exit System (EES) border kit in 2 lots. Lot 1: 75 outdoor EES-compatible facial-image capture devices (+4 option) and 75 managed 8-port switches (+4 option). Lot 2: 16 self-service EES data-capture kiosks (+4 option), 8 ABC (automated border control) e-gates and switches. CPV 35125110 (biometric sensors), additional 35123000, 30214000, 31644000, 32324100, 48810000. EKR002342252025; the notice was reissued repeatedly with the deadline moving 16/06 -> 07/07 -> 21/07 -> 28/07/2026 (TED 404740-2026, 470980-2026, 497245-2026). Final deadline 28/07/2026 12:00 CEST, bid validity 60 days.
signals.implies: Adjacent to Printec's self-service kiosk and digital-onboarding/eKYC (biometric capture, face and fingerprint enrolment) capabilities - the same kiosk hardware and identity-capture software stack, sold to a state buyer instead of a bank. Three deadline extensions suggest a thin bidder field. Now closed; the award notice will name the Hungarian biometric-kiosk integrator worth partnering with or displacing.
signals.followup: Poll EKR/TED for the result notice on EKR002342252025 to name the winner; the same integrator is the likely competitor for any Hungarian bank eKYC/self-service kiosk deal.

signals.signal: The absolute freeze on removing existing ATMs was relaxed. Under the government decree on emergency maintenance of ATM operation (in force from 07/06/2025; 129/2025 (VI. 5.) replaced the repealed 49/2025 (III. 24.)), a bank may relocate an ATM provided at least one working machine remains in that settlement or district; where technical constraints prevent an in-place upgrade the replacement must go elsewhere in the same settlement/district; and removal is permitted to redeploy to an underserved area, to rebalance within the same location on demand statistics, or on termination of the site lease.
signals.source_name: biztosdontes.hu, 'Fontos valtozasok az ATM-ek korul: megszuntethetok lettek a mar mukodo automatak' (summarising the Magyar Kozlony decree)
signals.implies: Creates a genuine fleet-churn opportunity: banks can now legally move and replace machines, so Phase-2 compliance can be met partly by relocating urban units - which in turn drives refurbishment, re-siting, re-installation and re-certification work. That is services revenue for Printec even where no new box is sold, and it explains why Budapest lost 8 ATMs while rural counties gained.
signals.likelihood: Already in effect; relocation activity visible in the 2025-2026 MNB county data
signals.followup: Verify the exact text of 129/2025 (VI. 5.) Korm. rendelet on njt.hu (njt.hu timed out this run) and quantify how much of the rural growth was relocation versus new units.

signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) - recurring cyber/monitoring procurement stream
signals.signal: MNB's 2026 EKR pipeline (55 notices to 28/07/2026) is dominated by IT security and monitoring rather than cash infrastructure: 'Kiberbiztonsagi technologiai kockazat monitorozas' (cybersecurity technology risk monitoring) tendered three times in 2026 (KE 4166/2026 awarded 21/04/2026; KE 9495/2026 published 03/06/2026, awarded 22/07/2026), QRadar licence support (KE 10593/2026, TED 434728-2026), Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR (TED 477302-2026), Google Threat Intelligence Standard (TED 412201-2026 / 490413-2026), Kiteworks (TED 389782-2026). No banknote-processing, sorting or ATM procurement appears anywhere in MNB's 2026 EKR record.
signals.source_name: EKR public notice register, full CSV export for contracting authority 'Magyar Nemzeti Bank'
signals.implies: Two things for Printec: (a) the central bank's security spend is monitoring/SOC-shaped, adjacent to Printec's transaction-monitoring and AML/compliance line but currently served by pure-play cyber vendors; (b) MNB is NOT buying banknote sorters or cash-processing equipment in this cycle, unlike HNB Croatia, NBS Serbia and Banka Slovenije - so there is no Hungarian central-bank cash-automation opening to chase right now.
signals.likelihood: Cyber-monitoring re-tenders roughly annually; no cash-equipment tender visible
signals.followup: Set a quarterly EKR poll on ajanlatkeroNeve=Magyar Nemzeti Bank to catch any future banknote-processing or cash-logistics tender early.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run for Hungary/EKR (no checkpoint existed). Method: (1) defeated the EKR Angular SPA by pulling the Angular bundle from https://ekr.gov.hu/main.<hash>.bundle.js and extracting the undocumented public API - https://ekr.gov.hu/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek (params eljarasTargya, ajanlatkeroNeve; page size hard-capped at 10) and the unpaginated CSV export at /api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek/exportalas/csv. (2) Ran 20+ Hungarian keyword sweeps and full CSV exports for Magyar Nemzeti Bank (1,024 notices), Magyar Posta (383) and the keywords 'automata' and 'ATM'. (3) Confirmed the prompt's warning: 'ATM' in EKR = Air Traffic Management (HungaroControl only). (4) Primary law/regulator route: downloaded and text-extracted the consolidated MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.) and MNB's 07/08/2025 cash-handling methodological guide from net.jogtar.hu and mnb.hu with pdfminer.six. (5) TED notice PDFs pulled and extracted for 511411-2026 (MNB HSMs), 424870-2026 (BKK POS award) and 497245-2026 (ORFK biometric kiosks). (6) Hungarian-language press cross-checks (Telex, Index, Bankmonitor, mfor, Penzcentrum, Bank360, biztosdontes) for the mandate's political status, MNB fleet statistics and the Constitutional Court case. Genuine gaps: (a) no Constitutional Court decision has been published on the ATM law and the Court's own case search is JS-rendered, so the case status rests on press plus the absence of any decision - it is reported as pending, not decided; (b) Annex 1 of MNB 19/2025 (the settlement-by-settlement package list) was not extracted line by line, so the per-bank counts are cited from press summaries of the decree, not counted from the annex; (c) njt.hu timed out repeatedly, so the exact text of government decree 129/2025 (VI. 5.) is cited from a secondary summary; (d) commercial-bank ATM procurement is legally invisible - it is not a search failure, it is the finding.
access_issues: ekr.gov.hu/portal is an Angular SPA that returns only a shell to plain GET - solved via the public JSON API and CSV export described above (no block logged). Date-range query params on that API are silently ignored; page size capped at 10, so CSV export is the only way to get full result sets. njt.hu (Nemzeti Jogszabalytar) returned connection reset/timeout on both https://njt.hu/jogszabaly/2025-19-20-2C and desktop-UA retries - worked around via net.jogtar.hu/getpdf. net.jogtar.hu/getpdf?docid=A2500020.MNB returned a 121-byte non-PDF (amending decree not served standalone). alkotmanybirosag.hu/kereses and /a-testuleti-ulesek-napirendje are JS-rendered and returned no case data to the fetch tool; public.mkab.hu serves binary PDFs that the fetch tool could not parse. Claude-in-Chrome was not connected in this run, so the Constitutional Court case register could not be escalated to a browser.
operator_requests: 1) Constitutional Court (Alkotmanybirosag) case register - an operator with a browser should search alkotmanybirosag.hu/ugykereso for 'automata bankjegykiado' / '2025. evi XVIII.' to retrieve the official case number(s) for the OTP/Erste/Raiffeisen complaint and any procedural order, since the site is JS-only. 2) Annex 1 of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.) - the settlement-by-settlement, bank-by-bank package list, ideally as published in Magyar Kozlony 2025/78 or later, to build a targeted Phase-2 site list.
